blocks.returns_en: A pre-implementation review of a plan or policy text: the holes it finds (each with a kind, a location, a reason and a severity) and alternative approaches that would avoid them.
blocks.read_en: The `holes` pointer in the returned JSON points to `review.json`; open it under the directory printed on the `works-factory: 記録の置き場:` line (or `terminal_record.artifacts.root` in `workflow get <run> --json`) and read its `faces` list.

inputs.proposal_file: Path to a text file holding the plan or policy text to attack before anything is written. It is read as plain text, even when its content is JSON.
inputs.purpose: The goal in one sentence. Empty means no goal is given.

example.purpose: State the goal in one sentence

measured.model: Claude Opus, effort high (model group wf-plan-review)

blocks.returns_en: Whether the goal's question stands, and if it does, an ideal design drawn only from the goal and the constraints, as a list of elements.
blocks.read_en: The `design` pointer in the returned JSON points to the design file; open it under the directory printed on the `works-factory: 記録の置き場:` line (or `terminal_record.artifacts.root` in `workflow get <run> --json`). Compare its elements with your own design to find what you left out or assumed.

inputs.constraints: A JSON array of measured constraints, each `{text, measured_how, kind}`. Empty means none.

example.purpose: State the goal in one sentence

measured.model: Claude Opus, effort high (model group wf-plan-review)

blocks.returns_en: The numbers, sizes, counts and exists-or-not claims in the request lines, measured again in the target, each with the command that was run and its output.
blocks.read_en: The `constraints` pointer in the returned JSON points to `premises.json`; open it under the directory printed on the `works-factory: 記録の置き場:` line (or `terminal_record.artifacts.root` in `workflow get <run> --json`). Each row is a measured fact; picking the rows that contradict your text is up to you.

inputs.request: A JSON array of request lines, each `{where, text}`. The claims to measure are in `text`.

measured.model: Claude Sonnet, effort medium (model group wf-judge-materials)

blocks.returns_en: The points already settled in the target's decision records (documents, ADRs and the like) that touch the request lines, so that a new text does not contradict them.
blocks.read_en: The `material` pointer in the returned JSON points to `material.json`; open it under the directory printed on the `works-factory: 記録の置き場:` line (or `terminal_record.artifacts.root` in `workflow get <run> --json`). A contradiction is described in the `detail` text of a point; there is no separate flag.

inputs.request: A JSON array of request lines, each `{where, text}`.
inputs.entry: Where the text came from, in one sentence. Empty means the run does not start from a judgment.

measured.model: Claude Sonnet, effort medium (model group wf-judge-materials)

blocks.returns_en: Each request line restated as a problem class without the proposed approach, compared with established practice quoted from primary sources, with a verdict of same or different for each class.
blocks.read_en: The `rows` pointer in the returned JSON points to `world.jsonl`, one row per class; open it under the directory printed on the `works-factory: 記録の置き場:` line (or `terminal_record.artifacts.root` in `workflow get <run> --json`). A row whose `versus.verdict` is `differs` is a finding; a row with `basis: knowledge` has no source and rests on the model's knowledge.

inputs.request: A JSON array of request lines, each `{where, text}`.
inputs.purpose: The goal in one sentence. Empty means no goal is given.
inputs.web: `on` searches the web for sources; `off` searches nothing and writes from knowledge only.

measured.model: Claude Opus, effort high for one node and Claude Sonnet, effort medium for two (model groups wf-judge-core and wf-judge-materials)

blocks.returns_en: The request lines cut into root-cause units, each with a label, a disposition, a prescription and a way to count the defect, plus the questions that need a human answer.
blocks.read_en: The `judgment` pointer in the returned JSON points to the judgment file, and the returned `units` and `questions` summarise it; open the file under the directory printed on the `works-factory: 記録の置き場:` line (or `terminal_record.artifacts.root` in `workflow get <run> --json`).

inputs.request: A JSON array of request lines, each `{where, text}`. An empty array means no request lines.
inputs.request_origin: Where the request lines came from, in one sentence.
inputs.purpose: Path to a purpose file `{purpose_text, source, known_weaknesses, source_files}`. Empty means no goal is given.

measured.model: Claude Opus, effort high (model group wf-judge-core)
